We need to propose retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable disconnections. The target: a sulfonamide linking a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) to a phenyl sulfonyl attached to a phenylacrylamide (trans). Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to para-phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl (aryl sulfonamide) attached to a phenylacrylamide (trans). Could be built via sulfonylation of an aniline with a sulfonyl chloride, then a Heck coupling to install the C=C-CO-NH-Ph? Actually the C=C-CO-NH-Ph is a cinnamamide attached to the phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl). So maybe start from 4-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and an aniline derivative (the other phenyl with amide). The other phenyl is a phenyl with a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph substituent at para position? Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So we have p-tolyl (C) attached to sulfonamide N, which is attached to sulfonyl group attached to phenyl (c2ccc...). That phenyl has a para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which has an NH2 at para? Wait Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an NH attached to the phenyl (the amide nitrogen attaches to phenyl at position 1, and that phenyl also has an NH2 at position? Actually the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an NH at position 1 (attached to amide) and an NH2 at position? The first N is the amide N attached to the phenyl; the phenyl has an N substituent at the other end (the last N). So it's a diamino phenyl (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is attached to a 1-aminophenyl (aniline) which also has an NH2 at para? Actually the phenyl is "c3ccccc3N" meaning an aniline (para? not specified). The preceding "N" is attached to the carbonyl carbon: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which has an NH2 at the para position relative to the amide? Not sure.

Anyway, we can propose a route: Step 1: Form the amide via coupling of trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-3-phenylacrylic acid) with 4-aminophenylamine? Actually we need an amide linking carbonyl to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we could start from 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Not.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-aminobenzoyl chloride? Actually we need C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. Could be made by reacting trans-cinnamic acid chloride with 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine). That yields trans-cinnamoyl-p-phenylenediamide (one amide, other NH2 free). That matches the fragment.

So step 1: Prepare trans-cinnamoyl chloride (from trans-cinnamic acid). Then react with p-phenylenediamine (commercial) to give the amide with free NH2.

Step 2: Sulfonylation: Use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) to sulfonylate the free NH2 of the amide product, forming sulfonamide linking to p-tolyl. However the target has sulfonamide attached to the p-tolyl via N-SO2-Ph (the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the sulfonamide N). Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl (p-tolyl) on one side, and the sulfonamide N attaches to the other phenyl (the phenyl bearing the cinnamamide). So we need a sulfonyl chloride derived from p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait p-toluenesulfonyl chloride is TsCl: CH3C6H4SO2Cl. Reaction with the amine (the free NH2 on the amide product) yields the sulfonamide linking p-tolyl-sulfonyl to the amine. That matches.

Thus overall 2 steps: (1) amide formation, (2) sulfonylation.

Leaves: trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), p-phenylenediamine (commercial), p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). All likely cheap.

We need to ensure price total < $9999. Likely yes.

Now we need to produce JSON route with up to 3 steps. Each reaction node includes template_id. We need to find appropriate template IDs for amide formation (acyl chloride + amine) and sulfonylation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups formed/broken.

Let's search for amide formation template.
